correctness.rationale: Same-arm routes have lengths d,u−d+v,u−d+w and cross-arm routes have four affine candidate lengths. Integrating near-equality strips on all three same-arm regions and three unordered cross-arm rectangles yields the three stated polynomials; degeneracies a=b<c and a=b=c have different overlap geometry. In the a=b<c case the tied-shortest two detours on the long arm occupy product area (c−a)²/4, hence atom that amount divided by L². Independently discretized all route order-statistics on 300×300 arclength grids for (1,1.5,2), (1,1,2), (1,1,1) with ε=.01; errors were ~1.4e−4, 2.1e−4, 9.3e−7 respectively (grid-resolution error). Source proof supplies exact all-real-length bound on ε, not the grid.
